items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: And then the trombones, I had from Pittsburgh, Floyd Beatty

ctx.x: He was discovered by Don Redman in those days, and of course Shorty went on to become very famous playing for Duke, and unfortunately, he died a young man. But he had one of the most beautiful tones of that day on trumpet. And the lead parts that Harold played were

really classics.
And then the trombones, I had from Pittsburgh, Floyd Beatty -- we called him Stumpy, a little fellow, playing trombone.
